chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Khalaf ibn Hammam from Amr ibn Thabit from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A woman named Umm Taybah used to trim the pubic hair of women. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) called her and said to her, 'O Umm Taybah, when you trim, remove the excess lightly and do not be too thorough, for it is clearer for the complexion and more pleasing to the husband.'

key_terms.أَشِمِّي: Trim lightly or remove the excess (moderate removal).
key_terms.أُمُّ طَيْبَةَ: Umm Taybah, a woman known for her expertise in grooming.
key_terms.تَخْفِضُ: She trims or removes hair (specifically pubic hair in this context).
key_terms.تُجْحَفِي: Be thorough or remove completely (excessive removal).

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method for trimming pubic hair according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the Prophetic emphasis on moderation (*wasatiyyah*) in personal hygiene, specifically advising Umm Taybah to trim rather than completely shave to preserve skin clarity and enhance marital intimacy. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of deriving practical legal nuances from the Prophet’s specific instructions to women, linking physical grooming to spiritual and social well-being.
